established.fact: Probe22 printed benchmark: 11 nominal engines on 1,227 items x 18 langs (+30 EN sanity = 1,257 packs); surya is best non-Sarvam engine, overall CER 0.3849 (WER 0.5956). Later sheet-mean basis gives 0.3944 and weighted 0.3956 on 1,227 items (different bases, not errors).

Overall CER ranking (FINAL_REPORT basis): sarvam 0.2400 (54 calls, 3/lang, directional only), surya 0.3849, tesseract_bilingual 0.4853, tesseract_indic 0.4870, easyocr 0.4941, indicphotoocr 0.5586, paddleocr_indic 0.6562, rapidocr 0.6692, anuvaad 0.7114, doctr 0.8691.

Refresh basis (2026-09-29, sheet.csv 12,324 rows; supersedes FINAL_REPORT means): sarvam 0.2640 (n=54), surya 0.3944, tess_bil 0.4907, tess_indic 0.4918, easyocr 0.5013, indicphotoocr 0.5634, paddle 0.6629, rapid 0.6753, anuvaad 0.7153, doctr 0.8704.

Per-language winners (n>=50, CER): surya wins 9 (bn 0.476, brx 0.153-0.165, hi 0.220, kok 0.425, ks 0.589, mai 0.030, pa 0.145, sd 0.315, ur 0.623); tesseract family mr 0.205 and or 0.256-0.259; easyocr sa 0.168-0.175. as/doi/mni/sat/gu/ne have n<50 so no winner claim.
Only ~6 of 12 n>=50 winner cells lie in the 0.10-0.40 CER band; no local engine is under 0.4 on bn, kok, ks, ur, mni, sat. The packet claim '14/18 within band' is unsupported.

Surya wins by McNemar (CER<0.5 pass/fail): 67 wins/8 losses/42 ties overall; brx p<0.012, ks p<0.0006, kok p<0.008. Tesseract family 28/15/80, easyocr 36/15/66, indicphotoocr 33/27/63, doctr 6/77/40; sarvam 0/0/0 (n<30).

Surya emits 100% empty on sa (99-100/100 items; 129 empty of 1,257 overall = ~10.5%) and 11/20 mni; surya has no language-hint parameter. Root cause (coverage vs wrapper bug) is untested; routing sa to any Tesseract captures ~80% of the fusion-oracle gain (0.3944->0.3296).
The 'surya sa = NO Ol Chiki' explanation is mislabelled: sa is Sanskrit, Ol Chiki is sat. Surya 2 has no Ol Chiki support (sat honest-empty).

Weak scripts: no open engine emits Ol Chiki (0/1,755 outputs); sat/mni are Sarvam-only in our engine set. Nastaliq (ks/ur/sd) is 0.59-0.94 CER on all local engines. Sat/mni/ks cells have only n=2-3 Sarvam samples.
Script-mismatch/consensus routing gives exactly 0.0000 gain on Nastaliq (ks/ur/sd): wrong-but-Arabic output is invariant in script block; a dedicated Nastaliq recogniser is needed, not routing.

All four edge theses killed: akshara-validity argmax fusion over 10 engines CER 0.6766 vs surya-always 0.4190 (61% worse); script-mismatch router precision 95-100%, recall 0-5.2%, routing gain -0.0351 CER; per-script metric already in Sarvam; GT-purity gate was a bug.

Fusion ceiling reproduced (seed 20260926, 300 items): surya 0.4190, tess_bilingual 0.5230, per-item oracle 0.3213, gap 0.0977; sa explains 67-69% of the gap, ex-sa gap only 0.0328-0.0332. Earlier 0.4277/0.5229 pair was impossible and withdrawn.

Ensemble voting rejected (G-B12): on 115 clean-GT pages the full ensemble beats all singles on 0/115 and is worse than worst single on 115/115 (line-segmentation mismatch). Agreement of >=3 families is a precision marker only: 5-gram precision 0.598 vs 0.355 but recall 0.046.

Other measured negative gates: rapidocr has no Indic server rec weights (all ch_*; Chinese config 400/400 zero Indic chars); paddle server-det NO-GAIN; tessdata_best x PSM 0/12; 300-dpi empty rescue 0/10; doctr zoo is French/Latin only (0.000 Indic script ratio).

Abstention (empty prediction scored CER 1.0) inflates mean CER. Latest register: anuvaad 59.4%, paddle 56.1%, rapidocr 39.7%, surya 17.4%, tesseract family 8.2-8.4%, easyocr 3.3% (earlier draft 43.7/50.3/28.0/10.5 superseded). Report median CER plus abstain rate.

Engine speed (13,289 packs): surya 24.3 s/page (~36 h for 5,344; p90 ~107 h), indicphotoocr 17.1 s, paddle 11.4 s, easyocr 11.1 s, tesseract family 2.6 s (~3.8 h), rapidocr 0.40 s (~0.6 h). A different Mac log gives surya 16.3 s/page (~24 h); load/machine dependent.

Tesseract trio are NOT byte-identical (ERRATUM 2026-09-30): predictions differ on 857/1,227; openbharatocr==tesseract_indic on 1,225/1,227; tesseract_bilingual matches only 370/1,227. Independent engines = 9; tesseract family counts as 1 vote.

GT-tier stratification: pooled 'local leads 10/18' is a PDF-text-layer artefact. On human-verified pooled n=18 Sarvam 0.171 vs best-local 0.430 (2.51x; 3.70x vs surya-always); official_pair n=9 Sarvam 0.064 vs local 0.243; all 21 item-level local wins are in the PDF tier. Tiers must never be pooled.

Surya tier signal: pair-tier CER 0.5639 vs pdf-tier 0.3135 (gap 0.25) flags PDF-tier GT as favourable; ~45% of 'clean' South GT is legacy-font mojibake (52/115 clean pages bad); official South PDFs 0/23,001 clean.

Bodhan IndicOCR: IndicDocLayout 33M (PP-DocLayoutV3/RT-DETR, 37 classes, reading order) + IndicBlockOCR 0.8B (Qwen3.5-0.8B, Sarvam-30B tokenizer); printed EN+22 langs, handwriting EN+12 langs. Size ~0.8B (the '~3B' in LIVE_LATEST is wrong).

Bodhan own measurements (Mac MLX): 300 pair-gold CER 4-bit 0.4034 / bf16 0.4010 vs surya 0.5660 (printed bn/hi/sa only); sample-100 pages (n=99) CER 0.6878/0.6863 (poor); bench small_rep n=1,173 CER 0.0540 WER 0.1356, 0.52 s/crop. Gate 1 = CONDITIONAL PASS.

Bodhan advantage is subset dependent: sample-100 CER 0.688 and surya weighted 0.3956 on 1,227 items mean Bodhan is not uniformly better than surya; the 0.4034-vs-0.566 comparison is only on 300 printed pair-gold items. Page-level 0.69 vs crop-level 0.054 gap (O-1) is unexplained.

Vendor bench (Sarvam blog 2026-09-24, word-acc macro-22): Sarvam 2.1 87.39, Bodhan 84.94, Gemini 3.6 Flash 79.35, GCV 71.76, surya 69.96. Bodhan own IndicOCR-PR: Sarvam 86.6, Bodhan 86.2; 8 of 22 per-language winners flip between vendor benches. Not comparable to our CER.

Vendor per-language: sat Sarvam 53.91 vs Bodhan 68.30; ks 54.82 vs 48.04 (Bodhan card shows Bodhan ahead 52.2 vs 43.3 - bench-specific); mni 85.12 vs 82.85; or 80.01 vs 75.45 (Gemini 81.01 higher). Decisions must name the bench; these are DEAD-for-decisions until re-measured on our manifest.

OldScan 55.3 is the English-only olmOCR-Bench sub-score (Sarvam 2.1; Opus 5 54.0; Bodhan 45.8; surya 42.8 or 41.8 by source), not an Indic metric, and OldScan is not on probe22. Ledger itself conflicts on benchmark versions (LightOnOCR 84.7, Chandra 51.1).

Surya licence: code Apache-2.0, weights modified OpenRAIL-M; s2(c) forbids a competing product (no carve-out) and s8 share-alike extends to Output/derivatives. NOT cleared commercially; the $5M cap was never the blocker. Surya is evaluation-only, never shipped or used as label source.

Bodhan licence is Indic Open Model License v1.0 (commercial + fine-tune OK; attribution for user-facing product s2.2; hosted API needs prior written approval s3.1; internal-component use s3.2; same-licence derivatives). The 'Apache 2.0' in strategy docs is wrong; ledger cites CC-BY-SA-4.0 on one record - unresolved.

Other licence facts: tessdata from indic-ocr (Apache-2.0, includes sat and mni; quality untested) is the licence-clean sat/mni backstop; 600K Kashmiri OCR dataset on HOLD (card CC-BY-4.0 vs embedded research-only licence); EasyOCR .pth weight licence open; IndicPhotoOCR PARSeq/detector weight repos (STocr, SceneTextDetection) unverified.

IndicPhotoOCR script-ID is a ViT fine-tune (google/vit-base-patch16-224-in21k, 12 classes, MIT release repo anikde/STscriptdetect), not CLIP; it has NO Ol Chiki or Meetei Mayek class so it cannot route sat/mni. Routing must read the script from Bodhan output text via Unicode ranges.

Bodhan weights: boss HF access granted, downloaded 2026-10-01 (official bodhan-ai/indic-ocr @cd50d301, mlx-4bit @6882ee7a, mlx-bf16 @bb091d3a, 5.35 GB). Official PyTorch path is not yet run: vendor code asserts CUDA, parity vs MLX waits GPU day.

Mac MLX is not the product: portable rule R-13 - MLX only a Mac accelerator, shipped Bodhan = official weights on PyTorch, LoRA via PEFT on CUDA, an MLX adapter counts only after conversion plus PyTorch parity. The MLX install broke the shared venv (numpy 2.2.6 vs indicphotoocr pin numpy==1.26.4).

Quality gate/restoration evidence: PreP-OCR -63.9% to -70.3% CER only on Latin historical pages; super-resolution helps low-res but hurts high-res (Rawat 2021); classic Otsu beat deep denoisers on Level-2 runs; OpenCV deskew/denoise may harm thin-stroke ur/ks/sat. No Indic binarisation benchmark exists; the R4 ablation was designed, never run.

R4 adopt rule (frozen): arms A0 none / A1 deskew+Otsu / A2 deskew+Sauvola / A3 DocRes pilot (n<=8); adopt only if median dCER <= -0.03, 95% CI excludes 0, on >=2/3 frozen engines, no glyph-fidelity regression (dot audit), CPU <=60 s classical / <=3 min learned.

Post-OCR correction evidence: Bhandari 2026 CER hi 10.20->6.73, gu 6.10->1.39, mr 8.19->3.29; Sanskrit +23 pts. But the Devanagari byte-level corrector did not transfer across engines and ByT5 gains appear only on the engine trained on, so correctors must be trained on the target engine's own noise.

Layout + reading order is 8/10 evidence (IndicDLP 2512.20236: 119,806 images, 42 classes, MIT; dots.ocr 2512.02498). Multi-engine fusion beats singles only in aggregate (6/10); raw OCR confidence is an unreliable correctness proxy; adaptive engine SELECTION (+23.7% on 15k govt docs, Zhang 2026) is not voting.

Per-block frozen-detector fallback (B-07) design: run fallback engines on Bodhan layout crops, triggered by deterministic bad-output checks (empty, wrong-script share, invalid Unicode sequences such as vowel sign without base or double virama, repetition loop, low mean log-prob). A learned router reopens only if oracle gap >=0.02 CER (RQ-11).

Recipe consensus: harness-with-VLM is the dominant pattern; fine-tune OCR-specialised VLM beats from-scratch (Chitrapathak-2; Parichay 89.8% EM, Tesseract+LLM 21.22%); SFT then RLVR (RL only +0.08 in the PaddleOCR-VL ablation after CPT +0.69, SFT +0.63); data engineering over architecture (MinerU2.5-Pro +2.71).

Alternative open backbones are unmeasured on Indic: PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 (0.9B, Apache-2.0, OmniDocBench v1.6 96.33/96.01 by source, 109 langs, no Ol Chiki/Nastaliq claim); GLM-OCR 0.9B (94.62 v1.5; presence in v1.6 table disputed 94.71); dots.mocr 3B MIT (Old-scans 48.2); MonkeyOCRv2 0.7B. None has a published Indic OCR Bench score.

Quantisation and training guards: no 4-bit recogniser quant without parity (QARI 4-bit CER 3.45 vs 8-bit 0.091); no layout-mix in the line stage (QARI-v0.3 0.061->0.300); 4-bit vs bf16 on Bodhan overall delta only 0.0015, but multilingual calibration (Ol Chiki/Nastaliq/Mayek/Odia) is required; Nastaliq needs autoregressive decoder (CTC collapses).

Weak-cell data levers: 600k-ks-ocr (602K Kashmiri word images, 10.6 GB, arXiv:2601.01088; licence conflict, HOLD); Ol Chiki: only OFL font Noto Sans Ol Chiki, sat.wiki ~15.9k articles, FLORES 3,001 sents, gate >=80% script; Mayek: Noto + Eeyek (font-disjoint), HarfBuzz mandatory; NE-OCR Meitei Mayek 95.56% (CC-BY-4.0).

Printed specialists show sat/ks are solvable: IIIT-H Mozhi-LR Ol Chiki CRR 90.60 / WRR 96.58 and Kashmiri CRR 87.71 / WRR 93.80 (printed), vs Sarvam 53.91/54.82; but ScriptMoE and UniLipi do not cover Ol Chiki/Mayek/Kashmiri.

Official hackathon page: government/legal/citizen documents with complex layouts, low-res scans, handwriting, multilingual text; 6 focus areas incl. layout-preserving JSON + searchable PDF; '22 languages' appears nowhere on the page (self-imposed); no scoring formula or submission format published; 'accuracy, layout detection, multilingual handling' named as eval.

Product scaffold exists: product/ with schema, CLI, PDF writer, script ID, tesseract and bodhan recognisers; requirements CPU/CUDA base, MLX optional darwin-only, multi-stage Dockerfile. CPU dry run on 6 South pages produced valid JSON+PDF+MD but Bodhan was a stub; Tesseract tam/tel/kan works.

Make the Tesseract fallback licence-clean and script-routed: route by Bodhan OUTPUT Unicode ranges; use FAST models PSM3 only; add empty-output handling (7.8% empties, ml worst); needs boss-approved traineddata (asm ben guj mar nep ori pan san snd urd; sat/mni via indic-ocr Apache pack, quality untested).

Reject ensemble/voting text in v4; keep only an agreement/consensus flag as review triage; any router/selection layer is built only if the RQ-11 oracle gap is >=0.02 CER in some language, and is gap-gated (blanket routing measured -0.0351).

Resolve the Page Expert reality gap before claiming it: implement order-invariant page CER (O-1), explain 0.69 page vs 0.054 crop, and run the official PyTorch/CUDA Bodhan on the same 99 pages and 300 gold items to prove MLX parity (R-13).

Adopt a printed evaluation-discipline block: report median CER + abstain rate (not mean), Wilson 95% CI per cell, McNemar exact (CER<0.5 pass/fail, p<0.05, gap>3pt, n>=50 for winner claims), per-GT-tier (never pooled), same-scorer same-manifest runs; vendor numbers are directional until a transfer obituary passes.

Pre-register kill criteria for the printed side (Page Expert, router, restoration, post-correction): thresholds T1=0.05, T2=3pt, n<30 INCONCLUSIVE, smoke-test (5 items) and abort at >2x wall-clock, keep-baseline fallback; today only G-P1/G-SHIP exist.

Add a printed baseline panel to v4: surya (eval-only) and Tesseract-family per-language CER from probe22 with n and tier labels, plus Bodhan on the same manifest; state that all probe22 data is printed (1,283 items, print_or_hand=printed) so it cannot be handwriting-gate evidence.

Create explicit sat/mni cells: no open engine emits Ol Chiki or Meetei Mayek; Bodhan reads them (vendor 68.30 / 82.85) but unverified on our manifest. Decide route (Bodhan LoRA vs Tesseract indic pack vs R3 synthetic with real validation set); never train on Sarvam fill.

Add an R2 Nastaliq cell for ks/ur: bf16 not 4-bit for Perso-Arabic (B-01), raw + Arabic-normalised scoring (B-02, 3-8 pt artefact), autoregressive decoder, no akshara-aux loss; script routing gives 0.0000 gain, so a specialist trained on synthetic + a few hundred real lines is required (needs boss approval).

Run the R4 OldScan restoration ablation (A0-A3, 40 old-scan pages, adopt rule median dCER <= -0.03 with CI excluding 0 on >=2/3 engines, dot/matra fidelity audit) before enabling restoration; keep the quality gate conditional; build an own old-scan eval set since OldScan 55.3 is English-only.

Scope post-correction as a separate product-output stage (not the benchmark): train per-engine on Bodhan's own errors with synthetic corruptions, no bench items, include a faithfulness check (FaithC4: general VLMs rewrite text), paired bootstrap on a held-out split.

Add a speed/throughput budget: per-engine s/page table on target hardware and a timed 50-image dry run for the 5,344 test; surya-scale latency (24.3 s/page, ~36 h) disqualifies any heavy fallback; Bodhan 0.52 s/crop (Mac) must be re-timed on CUDA/CPU.

Fix engine hygiene before any coverage matrix: surya sa empties, paddle brx/doi mapping, legacy-font mojibake GT detector (52/115 'clean' pages bad), pack-count==manifest assertion; needs boss U5 approval to re-run.

Quantisation/serving policy for the Page Expert: keep recogniser at bf16 unless 4-bit parity per script; KV cache BF16 and ViT/projector high precision; calibrate on Ol Chiki/Nastaliq/Mayek/Odia before any AWQ/GPTQ; avoid NIM ($4.5K/GPU/yr) under the free-only rule.

Evaluate alternates only as post-freeze hedges with boss-approved downloads: PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 (Apache-2.0, 0.9B), GLM-OCR, dots.mocr for OldScan; head-to-head on the same Indic manifest, not on OmniDocBench numbers.

Use IndicDLP (MIT, 42 classes) for layout/reading-order sanity and per-block language ID (IndicLID, licence unverified); note same-script LID (bn/as/mni, hi/mr/sa/ne) is unsolved so do not assume script==language.

Repair the shared environment: MLX install pushed numpy to 2.2.6 and broke indicphotoocr (numpy==1.26.4) and openbharatocr pins; use separate venvs or container layers so the HW expert checkpoints load on CPU/CUDA.

Weak-cell data hygiene: tag licences (NC lineage UTRSet/Odia-lipi/IndicCorp; CC-BY-SA minority rule), keep 600K-KS on HOLD, require a real-scan validation set for any synthetic Ol Chiki/Mayek/Nastaliq (synthetic-only overstates), and track fonts (1 each for Ol Chiki/Mayek in tooling).
